en: Gravity on the Moon is exactly one-sixth as strong as Earth's gravity, making a 120-pound person weigh only 20 pounds there.
A single bolt of lightning can heat the surrounding air to 30,000 degrees Celsius, which is about five times hotter than the Sun's surface.
Light travels at exactly 299,792 kilometers per second in a vacuum, allowing it to circle the Earth about 7.5 times in one second.
Sound travels about 4.3 times faster in water, at 1,480 meters per second, than it does in air at 343 meters per second.
Absolute zero is the coldest possible temperature, reaching exactly minus 273.15 degrees Celsius, where all atomic motion completely stops.
A standard refrigerator magnet has a magnetic field strength of about 0.005 teslas, while a hospital MRI machine uses 1.5 to 3 teslas.
The coefficient of friction between rubber tires and dry asphalt is about 0.7, but drops to just 0.1 on slippery ice.
The Great Pyramid of Giza contains about 2.3 million stone blocks, each weighing an average of 2.5 tons, moved using inclined planes.
Doubling the speed of a moving car quadruples its kinetic energy, making a crash at 60 kilometers per hour four times worse than at 30.
A 2-kilogram boulder resting on a 10-meter cliff has 196 joules of gravitational potential energy before it starts falling.
A large scrap yard electromagnet can lift 10,000 kilograms of steel when turned on, but drops it instantly when turned off.
A 100-watt solar panel generates exactly 100 joules of electrical energy every single second when exposed to direct, bright sunlight.
